articles.title: Tom Cruise, totalmente irreconocible con su transformación más radical en el nuevo tráiler de 'Digger'
articles.text:
El tráiler final de Digger es todo lo que los fans de Tom Cruise podían esperar. Y, a la vez, la sorpresa más radical para aquellos que aún no tuvieran en el radar la nueva película del cineasta mexicano Alejandro González Iñárritu. El actor de Top Gun y el director de El renacido unen fuerzas en una comedia negra de acción que promete no dejar indiferente a nadie cuando llegue a los cines en apenas unas pocas semanas.
Tal y como se muestra en el tráiler, Tom Cruise interpreta a Digger Rockwell, un multimillonario terriblemente poderoso con una misión muy clara. Tiene que salvar el mundo de un peligrosísimo natural que, en realidad, él mismo ha ayudado a desatar. El destino de la humanidad está en juego y este engreído ricachón debe demostrar que aún tiene alma y puede convertirse en el salvador que el planeta necesita.
El humor absurdo y la sátira política son los dos ingredientes que mueven claramente el tráiler de Digger. La promesa del filme es sacar más de una carcajada en los espectadores. Pero, sobre todo, lo que llama la atención es el salvaje cambio físico de Tom Cruise. Hasta arriba de prótesis y maquillaje, el actor está irreconocible. Lejos de su habitual apariencia atlética y cuidada, aquí lo vemos como un hombre mayor, hinchado y casi calvo.
Mira el tráiler de Digger
Esta comedia apocalíptica al estilo Teléfono rojo, ¿volamos hacia Moscú? está coescrita por el propio Iñárritu junto a Alexander Dinelaris, Nicolás Giacobone, and Sabina Berman. En el reparto de Digger, además de Tom Cruise están nombres de la talla de Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg, Jesse Plemons, Sophie Wilde, Emma D’Arcy, Robert John Burke y Burn Gorman.
La incertidumbre con Digger es máxima. Por un lado, cuenta con una mente brillante como la de Iñárritu detrás. Y también con Tom Cruise, que desde hace años suele acertar en los proyectos que acepta protagonizar. Pero su premisa disparatada y su tono tan gamberro y alocado siembran la duda sobre si este experimento será un rotundo éxito que incluso pueda dar un vuelco a la carrera de premios o si, por el contrario, será una decepción que no aterrice como ellos esperan.
Digger se estrena en cines el 2 de octubre.

articles.title: Group of bipartisan lawmakers ask US government to ban several hack-for-hire firms | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A bipartisan group of U.S. lawmakers has asked the U.S. government to ban several hack-for-hire firms — companies that carry out cyberattacks on behalf of paying clients. The lawmakers accuse the firms of targeting Americans and abusing foreign courts to silence U.S. reporting on their activities.
Democratic senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, and Republican congressman Pat Harrigan, on Wednesday sent a letter to U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, urging him to add three Indian companies to the department’s economic sanctions “entity list.”
The list effectively bars U.S. businesses from transacting with a named entity, with the aim of restricting the companies from accessing critical technology needed to function, including software licenses and cloud infrastructure.
In the letter sent to Lutnick and shared with TechCrunch, the lawmakers say BellTroX, CyberRoot, and Sunkissed Organic Farms (which previously operated under its former name, Appin) have for more than a decade conducted cyberattacks and targeted espionage against Americans, business owners, and their lawyers, to “manipulate ongoing litigation.”
The lawmakers say that these mercenary hacking companies have stolen data from thousands of Americans, and accuse the hackers of an “aggressive censorship campaign” to suppress public awareness of their alleged activities.
“This coordinated effort effectively allows foreign entities to use foreign courts to keep the American public in the dark about cyber threats to their own country and undermines the fundamental constitutional rights of U.S. citizens,” the lawmakers said.
It’s not clear if the Commerce Department will add the companies to its entity list, and a spokesperson did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.
The letter’s request to add the companies to the entity list follows extensive reporting and media investigations on the hack-for-hire industry, documenting how hackers are paid to break into the inboxes and devices of executives, lawmakers, and military officials to gain an advantage in lawsuits or influence their outcomes.
One of the companies, Appin, previously secured a global court order from an Indian court forcing Reuters to take down its reporting on the company while Reuters appealed the order. The notice that appeared on the page at the time said that Reuters “stands by its reporting.” The order was later lifted and the report republished.
The digital rights group Electronic Frontier Foundation previously defended two news organizations, Techdirt and the MuckRock Foundation, from legal threats after Appin engaged in “a campaign of bullying and censorship seeking to wipe out stories” about the company’s involvement in mercenary hacking.
The lawmakers’ letter said that the hack-for-hire companies “operated at the behest of the Qatari government” and that their targets included a former senior Republican lawmaker.
Appin has been linked to Qatar before. Earlier reporting tied Appin to a campaign of cyberattacks against FIFA officials, reportedly directed by Qatar as part of an effort to protect its plans to host the 2022 World Cup.
A representative from the Qatari government in Washington, D.C. did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.
An email from TechCrunch to Anuj Khare, a director at Sunkissed Organic Farms, went unreturned.
Separate reporting by The New Yorker and digital investigative unit The Citizen Lab has also documented espionage activity by the two other hack-for-hire firms named in the lawmakers’ letter, BellTroX and CyberRoot.
TechCrunch sought comment from representatives at CyberRoot, but did not hear back prior to publication. BellTroX could not be reached for comment.

articles.title: Shuddh Swad is building a regional snacks brand using traditional household recipes, starting with Bihar’s thekua
articles.text:
Shuddh Swad is building a regional snacks brand using traditional household recipes
West Bengal-based Shuddh Swad makes preservative-free Bihari thekua and is now developing recipes for other regional snacks. It was founded just last year with an initial capital of Rs 10,000, but the bootstrapped brand has already clocked Rs 1 crore in revenue.
Every Bihari household makes thekua differently, and much of it disappears just a week after Chhath Puja.
Thekua is a deep-fried sweet snack offered as a sacred prasad during Chhath Puja, a festival dedicated to Surya, the sun god, and goddess Chhathi Maiya.
Recipes passed down through generations vary from one kitchen to another, changing even further as one goes beyond the region.
Ingredients get substituted for cost, proportions are altered for shelf life, and a snack once made fresh at home becomes something manufactured to last. What is sold as ‘traditional’ in many Indian cities is, in some cases, a version shaped more by commercial requirements rather than the original recipe.
Shuddh Swad co-founder Jayanta Karmakar encountered one such version when he was 16. During Chhath Puja, he ate thekua from a roadside stall and fell ill.
The illness passed, but it left him with a question. Thekua is a snack found in nearly every Bihari household during Chhath Puja. Then why did one have to choose between a cheap street version and an expensive one sold only once a year?
"After that experience, I felt a product so tied to our culture and memories was slowly losing its originality," says Karmakar. "All I could think was that if we brought back the original taste in a clean, accessible way, people would genuinely connect with it. That thought became the starting point for Shuddh Swad."
Karmakar founded Shuddh Swad in 2025 with Kailash Bouri in Adra, West Bengal. Bouri had dropped out of school and was selling water bottles at railway stations to support his family when Karmakar pitched the idea to him. Samir Ansari joined Shuddh Swad in August 2025 as CEO and strategist, taking on operations as the business grew.
Built around traditional recipes
Shuddh Swad wants to bring out regional Indian snacks in their traditional forms. The idea is to use recipes closer to the ones households used decades ago, rather than versions altered for cost or shelf life, while keeping hygiene and freshness a priority.
"For me, it means the same method and ingredients thekua was traditionally made with in our homes," says Karmakar. "We're not just making a snack; we're preserving a piece of our culture and childhood memory, and bringing it to people."
The founders see thekuas appeal across generations. Older buyers get a snack closer to what they grew up eating, while younger consumers, who often indulge on chips and other packaged snacks, get a traditional alternative.
Shuddh Swad currently sells three thekua variants: coconut and suji, coconut and jaggery, and elaichi (cardamom). Each variant is currently priced at Rs 299, discounted from a listed price of Rs 599, and is available in 250gm, 750gm, and 1.25kg packs.
The products are made with wheat flour, semolina, desi ghee, milk, dry coconut, and dry fruits. “We do not add any preservatives, liquids or additives,” says Ansari.
How the thekua gets made
The dough is shaped using a traditional wooden mould and then deep-fried, a process, Ansari says, is largely unchanged from the way thekua has traditionally been made at home. Machinery is used only where hand production would be impractical at scale. Workers wear gloves and hairnets throughout production, he adds. Manufacturing takes place at a single facility in Adra, West Bengal.
Ansari says 60-70% of the workforce is sourced locally. A third-party courier partner handles deliveries rather than an in-house fleet. Shuddh Swad sells through its own website as well as ecommerce sites Amazon, JioMart, Flipkart, and Meesho, and quick-commerce apps Blinkit and Instamart.
The startup has so far sold 40,000 units. It has crossed Rs 1 crore in revenue within its first year of operation, entirely through self-funding. Its founding team of 11 people has since grown to 40 employees.
Bootstrapped with plans to expand
Shuddh Swad has not raised institutional funding. The business was started with roughly Rs 10,000 as initial capital and has grown over time without an outside investor.
"The hardest part has been consistently making a traditional homemade product at scale without compromising its original taste," says Bouri. "Production, hiring the right people, maintaining quality, day-to-day operations, there was something new to learn at every stage."
The founders have appeared on Bharat Ke Superfounders, an OTT reality show built around Indian founder stories. Karmakar credits the platform for giving Shuddh Swad a larger stage for its pitch.
The company is entering a market that is sizeable and competitive. India’s ethnic foods market was valued at $5.7 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $10.8 billion by 2034, growing at 7.12% annually, according to IMARC Group.
Haldiram’s, Mithila Foods, Desi Tesi, and Meal of the Moment are among the brands selling packaged regional and traditional snacks at a national scale.
Shuddh Swad’s plan has two parts: one, recover traditional recipes in their original forms, and, two, take this approach beyond Bihar and West Bengal. The founders want to recreate recipes from 20 years ago, before ingredients were substituted or proportions were changed for cost considerations.
“In the coming days, we want to take all these snacks, check their quality against the old recipe, and launch them on our platform,” says Ansari.
Research and development is underway for snacks from other states.

articles.title: Apple Watch : une application inédite pour le sport en approche
articles.text:
Comme le rapporte MacRumors, le code de watchOS 27 a révélé une application inédite baptisée Readiness. Celle-ci pourrait être entièrement consacrée à la récupération physique. Mais cela n’est pas tout. Le code de watchOS 27 a également révélé une série de nouveautés pour les prochaines générations d’Apple Watch.
Une nouvelle application entièrement dédiée à la récupération physique ?
Le code de watchOS 27 fait directement référence à une application inédite baptisée Readiness, que l’on peut traduire par « Préparation » ou « Forme ». Le lanceur de watchOS 27 positionne cette application, distincte de l’app Signes Vitaux, juste après l’application Entraînement dans l’agencement par défaut de l’écran d’accueil. Par ailleurs, l’application compagnon Watch sur iOS 27 fait également référence à Readiness pour organiser ses applications.
Étant donné que l’application Readiness n’a pas encore été incluse dans une version bêta de watchOS 27, nous ne connaissons ni son interface ni ses fonctionnalités. Cependant, son nom laisse clairement entrevoir une application entièrement dédiée à la récupération physique. Pour l’instant, l’app Activité propose seulement quelques données liées à l’effort fourni pendant les entraînements. Une application entièrement dédiée à ce sujet serait donc la bienvenue. Enfin, notons que cette application est également désignée sous le nom de Cobalt.
De nouvelles fonctions pour les futures Apple Watch
Le code de watchOS 27 fait également référence à toute une série de nouveautés pour les prochaines générations d’Apple Watch. Tout d’abord, Apple aurait développé un nouveau système dédié au suivi de la musculation, capable d’enregistrer bien plus précisément le déroulement d’une séance de sport. Chaque série pourrait ainsi être détaillée individuellement, avec le nombre de répétitions, la charge utilisée, l’équipement sollicité, le côté du corps travaillé ou encore la durée de l’exercice. Une même séance pourrait ainsi regrouper plusieurs séries avec des charges et des répétitions différentes. Précisons que cette fonctionnalité est pour l’instant inactive dans les bêtas actuelles.
Ensuite, watchOS 27 fait référence à une nouvelle famille de capteurs optiques qui pourrait correspondre à un système de mesure de la fréquence cardiaque amélioré. Celui-ci bénéficierait notamment d’une électronique moins sensible au bruit, ainsi que d’une sélection plus flexible des canaux optiques.
Enfin, les prochaines Apple Watch pourraient également gagner en stockage. Les Apple Watch Series 12 et Ultra 4 seraient équipées de 128 Go, contre 64 ou 128 Go pour les modèles antérieurs. La fin de la capacité de 64 Go semble se confirmer sur la nouvelle génération d’Apple Watch. Apple devrait dévoiler officiellement ces nouveautés lors de sa keynote de la rentrée qui se tiendra ce 9 septembre 2026.

articles.title: OpenAI afirma haber resuelto uno de los Problemas del Milenio con su IA. La que se ha liado después es gorda
articles.text:
OpenAI afirma haber resuelto el problema de existencia y regularidad de Navier-Stokes, uno de los siete Problemas del Milenio planteados por el Clay Mathematics Institute y dotados con un premio de un millón de dólares. La compañía ha publicado tanto la demostración analítica como su formalización en Lean. Eso, cuidado, no significa que el problema esté oficialmente resuelto aún —falta el escrutinio de la comunidad matemática—, pero antes de eso se ha generado una gran polémica por el trabajo previo de matemáticos humanos. El mérito del descubrimiento, si es que lo es, queda ahora difuso.
Más allá de GPT-6 Astra. Para descubrir esa teórica solución, OpenAI utilizó un modelo interno que describe como "significativamente más capaz" que el ya de por sí potente GPT-6 Astra, y que todavía están entrenando. Los responsables de este proyecto acabaron usando unos 10.000 agentes coordinados trabajando durante 88 horas y consumiendo varios millones de dólares en cómputo.
OpenAI no eligió este problema por las buenas. Tristan Buckmaster, matemático de la Universidad de Nueva York, y Levent Alpöge, matemático que trabaja en Anthropic, llevaban meses obteniendo avances importantes en problemas relacionados con este. Ellos tampoco partieron de cero, y de hecho su investigación continuaba una línea abierta por los matemáticos españoles Diego Córdoba y Luis Martínez-Zoroa.
La ciencia funciona y progresa así. Quienes buscan soluciones se apoyan en conocimientos y avances previos, y eso es justo lo que hizo en esencia OpenAI, que reconoce que empezó a atacar este Problema del Milenio cuando descubrió que Anthropic estaba logrando avances importantes. Aprovechar conocimientos públicos o líneas de investigación prometedoras no es en absoluto irregular y tampoco supone "hacer trampas".
Pero hay polémica. Buckmaster y Alpöge habían utilizado herramientas de IA, incluido Codex, durante su investigación, y de hecho Buckmaster escribió un comunicado planteando la posibilidad de que OpenAI hubiera podido beneficiarse de esas sesiones privadas. La compañía lo niega, y asegura que ni sus investigadores ni sus agentes vieron sus prompts, demostraciones o trabajo privado antes de que se hiciera público. A día de hoy no hay pruebas de que OpenAI "rebuscara" en sus conversaciones para encontrar la solución, así que esa acusación es solo eso: no está probada.
No sabemos qué pasó. En OpenAI sí indica que aunque lo considera improbable, no puede descartar que "datos anonimizados" derivados del uso que Buckmaster y Alpöge hicieron de Codex hubieran contribuido a mejorar sus modelos. Eso no significa que el modelo fuese entrenado con su demostración ni que pudiera recuperarla, pero sí implica que de momento no está claro dónde termina el uso privado de una herramienta de IA y dónde empieza ese aprendizaje que los modelos suelen aprovechar de esas conversaciones anonimizadas.
Quién se lleva el mérito. Buckmaster afirma que Sébastien Bubeck, de OpenAI, le propuso participar en la publicación del nuevo resultado dejando fuera a Alpöge, que precisamente trabaja para Anthropic, y critica la forma en la que se llevaron a cabo dichas conversaciones. Según Bubeck las cosas fueron distintas: no pretendían dejar a Alpöge fuera, y la idea era quién podía participar en una posible publicación de la demostración creada por el modelo de OpenAI. El enfrentamiento está servido.
Ahora las matemáticas son una cuestión de dinero. Que un laboratorio de IA se entere de que hay una línea de investigación prometedora y aplique miles de agentes de IA para resolverla empieza a convertirse en algo normal. Sin embargo hacerlo requiere inversiones enormes de dinero y plantea un dilema singular: ahora lo importante no es ya solo tener una buena idea, sino disponer de capacidad de cómputo para acabar de resolver el problema.

articles.title: Bouygues Telecom rafle l'exclusivité de la distribution des Honor Magic V6 et 600 Pro en France
articles.text:
Bouygues Telecom va devenir, dans quelques jours, le seul revendeur en France, hors Honor, des téléphones Magic V6 et 600 Pro. Une exclusivité qui doit permettre à l'opérateur de se démarquer sur le marché des smartphones premium.
Bonne nouvelle pour ceux qui attendaient des nouvelles des Magic V6 et 600 Pro d'Honor du côté des opérateurs français. Comme Clubic est en mesure de l'assurer ce mercredi 8 septembre 2026, c'est Bouygues Telecom qui a décroché l'exclusivité pour distribuer les deux téléphones sur sa propre boutique. L'opérateur promet des facilités de financement, une reprise de l'ancien mobile et un accompagnement pour faciliter la transition. De quoi mettre la main sur le pliant le plus fin du monde ou un clone d'iPhone à l'autonomie hors norme, sans passer par le site du fabricant.
Bouygues Telecom signe un accord d'exclusivité avec Honor pour le Magic V6 et le 600 Pro
Bouygues Telecom réussit un joli coup avec cet accord, puisqu'il devient le seul revendeur tricolore du Magic V6 et du 600 Pro, en dehors du site officiel de la marque chinoise Honor. Cette exclusivité totale sur deux smartphones aussi attendus, c'est assez rare.
Les clients pourront financer leur achat, faire reprendre leur ancien téléphone et profiter de l'accompagnement habituel de l'opérateur. « Nous permettons ainsi à nos clients de s'équiper des derniers modèles Honor à des conditions exceptionnelles, tout en bénéficiant de la qualité de service Bouygues Telecom », nous assure Marc Laurier, directeur marketing grand public de l'opérateur. Selon nos informations, les deux smartphones seront proposés à la vente sur le site internet de Bouygues Telecom dans les prochains jours tout au plus, peut-être même dès cette semaine.
Le pliant ultrafin d'Honor face au clone d'iPhone
Au rayon des pliants ultrafins, le Honor Magic V6 a de quoi impressionner. Il nous a agréablement surpris sur Clubic, du haut, si l'on ose dire, de ses 4 mm une fois déplié, et avec une batterie monstrueuse de 6 660 mAh, sans oublier la double certification IP68/IP69 (résistance à l'eau et à la poussière), une première sur ce format. Sous le capot tourne un Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 flambant neuf, épaulé par 16 Go de RAM. Facturé 2 299,90 euros acheté seul, il vise les amateurs de technologie pointue, prêts à mettre le prix pour un appareil déjà crédité de 9/10 chez nous.
On imagine qu'au jeu des forfaits et autres reprises ou remises, le Honor Magic V6 sera accessible à des tarifs plus raisonnables chez Bouygues Telecom.
Le 600 Pro est plus accessible, à 999 euros. Il mise sur un argument totalement différent, qui est une autonomie de près de 35 heures en usage mixte, portée par sa batterie silicium-carbone, une technologie qui gonfle la capacité sans épaissir l'appareil. Le tout est propulsé par un Snapdragon 8 Elite et un triple capteur photo emmené par un module principal de 200 Mpx, rien que ça. Son design est assez proche des derniers iPhone, il ne passera sans doute pas inaperçu chez les puristes d'Apple. Il ne manque en tout cas pas d'atouts.

articles.title: Apple Event 2026 live — new foldable iPhone Duo, AirPods 5, and more set to be announced
articles.text:
Apple Event 2026 live — new foldable iPhone Duo, AirPods 5, and more set to be announced
Apple's biggest event in years is underway
Apple's hotly anticipated ‘Surprise and Shine’ event is happening now, and we're on the ground in California bringing you all the big announcements as they happen.
Leading the list of rumored-to-be-unveiled products is Apple's first foldable iPhone — expected to be called either the iPhone Duo or iPhone Ultra — which, if it does arrive, would represent the biggest iPhone shake-up in recent history. This dual-screen device could also skyrocket the popularity of foldable phones more generally, so Samsung and Google executives are surely paying close attention.
Elsewhere, Apple looks set to refresh its wearable, earbud, and smart home lines with new Apple Watches, AirPods, and HomePods, respectively — and we may even see a new version of the Apple TV 4K, which hasn't been updated since 2022.
Proceedings kicked off at 10am PT / 1pm ET / 6pm BST — or 3am AEST on September 10 if you're in Australia — and you can follow along below for our live reaction to new CEO John Ternus' first-ever Apple Event.
Axel is TechRadar's Phones Editor, responsible for covering the latest hardware and software developments in mobile technology. He's written close to 2,000 articles for TechRadar on everything from iPhones to tri-folds, and so is well-placed to walk you through today's potentially historic Apple Event.
Apple Event 2026 — rumored announcements
- Foldable iPhone Duo (or Ultra)
- iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max
- Apple Watch Series 12
- Apple Watch Ultra 4
- AirPods 5
- Apple TV 4K (2026)
- HomePod mini 2
Apple Event 2026 — how to watch
Today's ‘Surprise and Shine’ Apple event is taking place at the Steve Jobs Theater in Apple Park, California, but you can follow along via the livestream video embedded above or via Apple’s official event page.
Proceedings kicked off at 10am PT / 1pm ET / 6pm BST, which is 3am AEST on September 10 if you're in Australia, but you'll be able to re-watch the stream once the event finishes (we're expecting things to wrap up around 12pm PT / 3pm ET / 8pm BST, or 5am AEST in Australia).
Live updates
First up is the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. "We made massive advancements in Intelligence, Performance, Battery, and Camera," Ternus says.
It comes in Black, Silver, Glacier, and Burgundy.
OK we really are getting straight into the new iPhones. I respect it!
We're kicking off with... iPhone?! I wasn't expecting that. Ternus says the iPhone represents the perfect intersection between AI and hardware. Private Cloud Compute delivers "personal intelligence that's actually personal."
Tim Cook officially hands the reins to John Ternus. Here we go.
And we're off. We're getting a 'Shot on iPhone' sequence to kick things off (classic!). $10 says Craig Federighi appears before it finishes.
Two mins to go. Good luck, folks — I hope you get every foldable iPhone you wished for.
Tim Cook is in the building
Former (which feels weird to write) Apple CEO Tim Cook is in the building for new CEO John Ternus' first big Apple Event. A penny for his thoughts...
Lance and Jake have taken their seats inside the Steve Jobs Theater. It's getting real now.
The current foldable competition
Switching focus back to Apple's first foldable iPhone, there are currently three similarly sized devices available on the market right now: the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, the Xiaomi 18 Fold, and the Huawei Pura X Max.
The first of that trio is the big competition for the iPhone Duo/Ultra. The Z Fold 8 is available globally, and it's been well-received by reviewers and customers as a sturdy, pocket-friendly phone designed for content consumption above all else. Apple will surely ensure its foldable iPhone one-ups the Z Fold 8 in some way, but we're not sure how just yet. I'm banking on a less-visible crease or a superior camera array.
The Xiaomi 18 Fold and Huawei Pura X Max are only available in China, but both may look more similar in appearance to Apple's foldable iPhone than the Galaxy Z Fold 8. Both phones have two rounded corners when closed and four when open, while Samsung's phone is straight-edged whichever way you slice it.
Just 45 minutes to go — Lance and co. are being ushered into the Steve Jobs Theater to take their seats.
Look out for new health-tracking software
While both new Apple Watch models will almost certainly get hardware upgrades, Apple is also expected to unveil new wellbeing tracking tools for health-minded users. A new default Readiness app is expected to launch for the Apple Watch home screen, delivering a new and improved recovery experience for users — because what you do after a workout is just as important as the workout itself.
The Workout app could be getting an overdue facelift, too. The new version will reportedly let you record individual reps and sets for strength routines to help you keep track of your progress. I’ve been using my iPhone's Notes app in the gym for years, so this is one feature I’m hoping will make an appearance at today's event.
Another handy health tool we’re expecting to see unveiled is always-on heart rate data tracking, which will monitor your activity and recovery over 24 hours using only your heart rate. This sounds exciting, but given that only the Ultra 4 is expected to get new sensors, it’s likely that this feature will be exclusive to Apple's most premium wearable.
The premium Apple Watch Ultra is also tipped to get another update today, but again, it won't necessarily look any different from the current model. Some speculate that the Watch Ultra 4 will be identical in appearance to the Watch Ultra 3, while others claim it will have a bigger screen and slimmer build.
Of course, the biggest updates will likely come under the hood, with the Watch Ultra 4 set to get a new chipset — a no-brainer given Siri AI’s imminent rollout — and a suite of new sensors for more accurate health tracking.
Watch out for watches
The foldable iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro won't be the only stars of today's event: Apple Watches also look set to get an overhaul, starting with the Apple Watch Series 12.
Now, if you're expecting major design upgrades, prepare to be disappointed. According to the latest rumors, the Series 12 will look similar to its predecessor, the Apple Watch Series 11 — though one rumor does hint at ceramic case options, which would be a nice touch. We’ve also heard that the Series 12 could have a new LTPO display instead of the classic OLED, but we’re taking this claim with a pinch of salt.
For now, we’re expecting the biggest upgrades to come inside the watch. Specifically, the Series 12 is tipped to house Apple’s new S12 chipset, which should be powerful enough to support Siri AI, as well as a larger battery for a much-needed battery life boost.
The sun is out at Apple Park! Incidentally, it was raining cats and dogs during last year's event, so perhaps the universe is telling us we're in for a more exciting set of announcements in 2026.
And here's part 2 of the pair's predictions:
Here's Lance and Jake on their predictions for today's event:
Just two hours to go! A reminder that today's event kicks off at 10am PT / 1pm ET / 6pm BST (or 3am AEST if you're in Australia, but if you're reading this from Sydney: go back to sleep).
OK, I'm pretty sure I know what the winning response will be (it rhymes with "grindstone culture"), but cast your vote below for your most anticipated announcement from today's Apple Event:
The Boys Are Back in Town
Lance has now been joined by Jacob Krol, TechRadar's US Managing Editor for News. Between them, they'll be bringing you hands-on impressions and videos of everything Apple is announcing today — including, we hope, the company's first foldable iPhone.
TechRadar's Editor at Large, Lance Ulanoff, has touched down in Apple Park. His first stop? The official Apple Store, which appears to be temporarily boarded up in preparation for new products.
In terms of what won't be unveiled today, we're not expecting Apple to announce new MacBooks, iPads, or Vision Pro-style VR hardware. Software upgrades will most likely take a backseat, too, after iOS 27, Siri AI, and WatchOS 27 were all announced at WWDC 2026 back in June (though it's worth noting that these new OS packages will almost certainly be released alongside their corresponding hardware products in September).
Regarding Ternus' teaser post on X, some Apple fans are pretty convinced it refers to the iPhone 18 Pro's variable aperture, rather than the company's first foldable iPhone. Perhaps we'll get a second teaser video before the event kicks off at 10am PT / 1pm ET / 6pm BST?
The Apple Store is down
Oh, and the Apple Store website is now closed for maintenance, which typically happens right before the company refreshes its product lineup. Not long to go now!
First official look at the iPhone Ultra?
New Apple CEO John Ternus has just posted what appears to be a tease for one of the company's new iPhones on X. There's no Tim Cook-style "Good morning!" here, nor even a reminder of today's event start time. Instead, Ternus has shared a 14-second clip of a spotlight shining down on the corner of what looks like an iPhone. Is this a hint that the iPhone Ultra/Duo won't have four straight edges à la the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, or a reference to the rumored variable aperture feature on the iPhone 18 Pro?
Thinking of selling your iPhone 17 Pro? Do so ASAP
Here's some last-minute advice for you: if you're planning on selling your current iPhone 17 Pro or Pro Max to fund an upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro line, you should head out to your local tech store and do so ASAP. Why? Because current iPhones could fall in value by up to 30% once the new models launch.
“Many people will make the mistake of waiting to see what new features the next iPhone range has before trading in their old device, but our data clearly shows that waiting just a few weeks could mean a significant hit on the amount customers can get for it," Joe Armstrong, Head of Trading at musicMagpie, tells TechRadar. "Those who wait until October may see handsets drop by an average of £48 and up to £122."
It's the same story in the US and Australia, and while Armstrong references October as the hard trade-in deadline, your absolute best bet is to sell your current iPhone before 12pm PT / 3pm ET / 8pm BST today.
Of course, selling before the iPhone 18 Pro has even been announced would leave you with no phone until the new models begin shipping later this month, but some retailers will allow you to lock in a sale price today and keep using your phone for a few more weeks. That's the ideal scenario during this precarious time of year for iPhone trade-in values.
Back to the iPhone Ultra/Duo/whatever you want to call it, let's talk about what features it reportedly won't have. According to various rumors, there's a chance Apple's first foldable will lack Face ID, a telephoto camera, MagSafe, the Action button, and a physical SIM card slot.
Now look, I can live without the Action button, a SIM card slot, and a telephoto camera, but no Face ID or MagSafe? I'm not sure I would spend $2,000 on an iPhone without those two features, which feel pretty essential to how I use my iPhone every day.
Don't forget about the iPhone 18 Pro
A quick word on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, which will likely be the forgotten children of today's Apple Event while also being the best-selling Apple products of the next 12 months.
Gurman says both phones will have smaller, more functional Dynamic Islands, an upgraded vapor chamber (read: they won't get as hot), and "major" new camera hardware. Rumors suggest a variable aperture feature could be chief among this new hardware, which would make the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max some of the best camera phones around.
A clear message from Samsung
If you walk around London, New York, or Seoul today, you may spot Samsung's new tongue-in-cheek advertising campaign, dubbed ‘Welcome to Foldables’.
The Galaxy Z Fold 8 manufacturer is clearly hoping to remind people that it has spent a decade developing foldable technology, and that Apple — if it does release its first foldable today — is late to the party.
That said, Samsung isn't totally against Apple's late entry into the foldables market. Speaking to Bloomberg last year, Samsung's President and COO of the company’s Mobile eXperience (MX) division, Won-joon Choi, said: "I think healthy competition with other companies will bring more innovations, and then bring more benefits to consumers. So we are welcoming others to join this category, which we created back in 2019 [...] Having another global company join this category, I think it's good for the industry, and also, it's going to be great for consumers."
Today might also be the day we finally get a successor to the HomePod mini. This smaller, more affordable version of the standard Apple HomePod (which now exists as the HomePod 2) was released way back in November 2020, but hasn't been updated since.
More than 20 (!) new iPhones have launched in that same period, so to say the HomePod mini 2 has been a long time coming would be an understatement.
Rumored upgrades for the HomePod mini include a faster chipset (duh!), superior audio quality, and Siri AI functionality.
Let's talk AirPods
Moving away from the iPhone for the moment, let's talk AirPods. Today, we're expecting Apple to announce two new AirPods models: the AirPods 5 without ANC (active noise cancellation), and AirPods 5 with ANC.
Both models are set to use Apple's new H3 chipset, which should improve audio processing and reduce latency, though it remains to be seen how different the AirPods 5 with ANC will be from the AirPods Pro, which already offer ANC.
In any case, we're not expecting to see any camera-equipped AirPods launch today, despite rumors suggesting that such a product is indeed in development.
Another important note: Gurman says Apple's first foldable iPhone will have Apple Pencil support. Steve Jobs won't be happy...
Gurman adds in the same X post that the iPhone Duo will have a starting price of $2,000, rising to $3,000 for the 2TB model. And, yes, in case you were in any doubt: those numbers would make the Duo the most expensive iPhone of all time.
Could the iPhone Ultra be the iPhone Duo?
According to seasoned Apple tipster Mark Gurman, the iPhone Ultra will in fact be called the iPhone Duo. It's pretty hard to believe that such a drastically different name has emerged just hours before the product itself is due to be unveiled — so we're still a tad skeptical about its authenticity — but Gurman has an excellent track record when it comes to Apple predictions.
Of those nine rumored products, the most hotly anticipated is Apple's first foldable iPhone, which we've been referring to as the 'iPhone Ultra' for close to a year now. But at the very last minute, the rumor mill has spat out an unexpected new name for this folding device...
First, a quick reminder of what's happening: Apple's ‘Surprise and Shine’ event is scheduled to start at 10am PT / 1pm ET / 6pm BST today (that's 3am AEST on September 10 if you're in Australia).
This is the 2026 edition of Apple's annual product showcase, and we're expecting to see as many as nine (yes, nine) new products unveiled.
Good morning, folks! It's Apple Day — the most important date in the annual tech calendar and the busiest day of the year for the TechRadar office (sigh).
I'll be bringing you the latest iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch rumors ahead of the event's kick-off later today, and trust me: there's a lot to cover.

articles.title: Google warns of new Chrome zero-day bug exploited in attacks
articles.text:
Google has patched 230 vulnerabilities on Tuesday, including another actively exploited Chrome zero-day bug, the seventh such vulnerability patched since the start of the year.
"Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-87491 exists in the wild," the company said in a Tuesday security advisory.
The company began rolling out patched versions to Windows (153.0.8010.36), Mac (153.0.8010.37), and Linux (153.0.8010.36) systems in the Stable Desktop channel two days after Jihyeon Jeong, a research intern at Seoul National University's Compsec Lab, reported it to Google.
Google says the security update could take days or weeks to reach all Chrome users worldwide, but it was available immediately when BleepingComputer checked for updates earlier today.
Those who prefer not to update manually can rely on Chrome to automatically check for updates and install them at the next launch.
This high-severity zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-87491) stems from an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Chrome V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, which remote attackers can exploit to execute arbitrary code inside the web browser's sandbox via crafted HTML pages.
Successful exploitation can also let them access data beyond the memory buffer through heap corruption, exposing sensitive information or triggering a crash.
While Google said it was aware of CVE-2026-87491 zero-day exploits used in the wild, the company has yet to share further details about these attacks.
"Access to bug details and links may be kept restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix," Google said. "We will also retain restrictions if the bug exists in a third party library that other projects similarly depend on, but haven't yet fixed."
Since the start of the year, Google addressed five more actively exploited zero-days:
- An iterator invalidation bug (CVE-2026-2441) in CSSFontFeatureValuesMap (Chrome's implementation of CSS font feature values), which Google addressed in mid-February.
- Two other Chrome zero-day bugs exploited in attacks in March: an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Skia 2D graphics library (CVE-2026-3909), and an inappropriate implementation vulnerability in the V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine (CVE-2026-3910).
- A use-after-free weakness in Dawn (CVE-2026-5281), the underlying cross-platform implementation of the WebGPU standard used by the Chromium project, which Google patched in April.
- And a type confusion flaw in V8 (CVE-2026-85046) fixed earlier this month.
Google fixed eight other zero-days exploited in the wild in 2025, many of them reported by its Threat Analysis Group (TAG), known for tracking zero-day exploits used in spyware attacks.

articles.title: Chipmaker Patch Tuesday: Nvidia, AMD, Arm Issue Security Advisories
articles.text:
Major chipmakers AMD, Arm, and Nvidia published new security advisories on Tuesday to notify customers of vulnerabilities recently discovered in their products.
AMD announced fixes for CVE-2026-43603, a NULL pointer dereference flaw in its Linux GPU kernel driver that could lead to system crashes and a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
The company credited Maxime Rossi Bellom and Ramtine Tofighi Shirazi from SecMate for reporting the security defect.
“According to the researchers’ report, when an application invokes a specific graphics memory management interface to perform a ‘clear’ operation under certain compute-processing conditions, the driver may fail to validate an internal data reference before use,” AMD notes in its advisory.
The company rolled out fixes for EPYC Athlon, Ryzen, Radeon, and Instinct processors in July. It plans to release the patches for the EPYC Embedded and Ryzen Embedded processors in October.
Arm published an advisory covering nine vulnerabilities in its Mali GPUs that could allow access to already freed memory or to sensitive kernel information, or could lead to a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
The company has released fixes for the Valhall GPU and Arm 5th Gen GPU Architecture kernel and userspace drivers. The Bifrost GPU kernel and userspace drivers are also affected.
Nvidia announced a software update for the Triton Inference Server for Linux that resolves two high-severity security defects. The first could lead to a DoS condition, while the second could lead to information disclosure, data tampering, and DoS conditions.
At the time of publishing, Intel had not released new security advisories since the previous Patch Tuesday.

articles.title: Apple Surprise and Shine event, what to expect today
articles.text:
Table of contents
Apple is holding its fall hardware event today, Wednesday, September 9, 2026. Apple calls it “Surprise and Shine.” The keynote starts at 10 a.m. Pacific Time (1 p.m. Eastern) (6:00 p.m WAT), and it streams live from Apple Park in Cupertino, California.
This is Apple’s first big event under a new boss, John Ternus, who resumed as CEO on September 1, eight days before this keynote. Ternus spent more than two decades at Apple and led its hardware engineering team for five years before stepping into the top role. This keynote is his first major product presentation as CEO.
Here is everything you need to know ahead of the event:
When the Apple Surprise and Shine event starts and how to watch it
The keynote begins at 10 a.m. Pacific time. You can watch it in a few ways:
- Apple’s official events website
- The Apple TV app
- Apple’s YouTube channel
- Any regular web browser on a Windows computer, an Android phone, or any other device
You do not need an iPhone or a Mac to watch. Apple usually leaves the full recording online once the live broadcast ends, so you can catch up later if you miss it.
Here is when the keynote starts in different parts of the world.
| Location | Local start time | Local date | 
| San Francisco | 10:00 a.m. PDT | September 9 | 
| New York and Toronto | 1:00 p.m. EDT | September 9 | 
| São Paulo | 2:00 p.m. BRT | September 9 | 
| London | 6:00 p.m. BST | September 9 | 
| Lagos | 6:00 p.m. WAT | September 9 | 
| Paris and Berlin | 7:00 p.m. CEST | September 9 | 
| Johannesburg | 7:00 p.m. SAST | September 9 | 
| Dubai | 9:00 p.m. GST | September 9 | 
| New Delhi | 10:30 p.m. IST | September 9 | 
| Beijing and Singapore | 1:00 a.m. | September 10 | 
| Tokyo | 2:00 a.m. JST | September 10 | 
| Sydney | 3:00 a.m. AEST | September 10 | 
What Apple is expected to announce
1. The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are the safest predictions on this list. Apple has refreshed its premium iPhones every September for years, and Reuters reported in June that both models were still on track for a September release. Screen sizes are expected to stay the same as last year, at 6.3 inches for the Pro and 6.9 inches for the Pro Max.
The bigger upgrade may sit inside the phone. Reports point to a new A20 Pro chip built on a smaller 2-nanometre manufacturing process, which should make it faster or more power-efficient without taking up more space. Apple may also add more memory to support its on-device AI features. None of this is confirmed yet.
The camera could see a more visible change. Several reports mention a variable-aperture system for the 48-megapixel main camera, which would let the lens open wider for more light or narrow for a sharper background blur. How much this actually improves your photos will depend on the sensor and lens Apple uses, along with its software, so the feature alone will not guarantee better pictures.
Other rumoured changes include a smaller Dynamic Island, bigger batteries, and slightly thicker bodies. Leaked dummy units point to black, silver, light blue, and dark purple colour options. Every detail here comes from reporting or leaks, not Apple, and colour plans can still shift before launch.
Price is one of the bigger open questions. Apple told investors earlier in 2026 that rising memory and storage costs were hurting its hardware margins, and Reuters reported that the company planned to raise prices to cover that gap. Since the iPhone 17 Pro already launched at a premium price in 2025, analysts expect the iPhone 18 Pro line to cost even more this year.
2. Apple’s first foldable iPhone
The foldable iPhone is the biggest possible announcement at this event. Recent reports describe a book-style phone that looks like a regular iPhone when closed, then opens into a small tablet screen. Analysts quoted by Reuters expect Apple to focus on hinge durability and a less visible crease across the folding display, since these two issues have shaped how people judge other foldable phones on the market.
Even the product’s name is still unclear. Most reports call it the iPhone Fold or iPhone Ultra, but a late Bloomberg report cited by The Verge says Apple may go with “iPhone Duo” instead. That same report puts the starting price at around $2,000 for the 256GB version, with a 2TB model possibly reaching close to $3,000. Reuters separately reports that analysts expect a price above $2,500. Because these numbers don’t agree, treat none as fact until Apple confirms a price on stage.
Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo previously described a 7.8-inch inner display and a 5.5-inch outer screen, alongside Touch ID built into the side button instead of Face ID, two rear cameras, and a body around 9 to 9.5 millimetres thick when folded shut. Later reports have repeated these numbers. Bloomberg’s most recent reporting adds side-by-side apps and iPad-style multitasking, plus Apple Pencil support. These details remain unconfirmed by Apple.
This device could matter well beyond its first year on shelves. Foldable phones made up only about 1.6% of global smartphone shipments in 2025, according to figures cited by The Verge. IDC research in the same report estimates Apple could capture 28% of foldable phone shipments in its first year alone, and an IDC analyst told Reuters that Apple’s foldable could bring in more than $45 billion in revenue by the end of 2027. These are forecasts for a product that has not launched yet, but they explain why so much attention is on this one device.
Apple is stepping into a space Samsung, Huawei, Google, and Motorola have built over several years. Its challenge is making the bigger screen worth the higher price and the added weight and complexity. A sturdy hinge and a barely visible crease would fix two common hardware complaints. That extra screen space is only useful if the software uses it well, and that becomes clear once people start using it.
3. The regular iPhone 18 may not arrive until 2027
Apple may skip its usual full lineup this September. Reuters and The Verge report that the standard iPhone 18 lineup, including the next iPhone Air and the cheaper iPhone 18e, could move to a spring 2027 launch instead. That would leave today’s event focused only on the Pro models and the foldable phone.
This split schedule would give Apple two iPhone sales seasons a year instead of one, and it would reduce how many new models go into mass production at the same time. A Reuters report from January said the change would help Apple manage the complicated production needs of its first foldable phone while putting more resources behind its premium devices. This timing for the standard iPhone 18 is still based on reporting, not an Apple announcement.
4. Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4
Apple is also expected to update both of its main watch lines today. Reports linked to Bloomberg say the company has tested the Apple Watch Series 12 in GPS and cellular versions, alongside a new Apple Watch Ultra 4. Both watches are expected to run on a faster S12 chip and lean more heavily into health and fitness tracking.
A big redesign looks unlikely this year. Bloomberg reported that the Series 12 may bring back a ceramic case option and add new band colours while keeping its current shape. Other leaks point to better optical sensors and continuous heart-rate tracking. There is also talk of more onboard storage, though these details carry less certainty than the fact that both watches exist.
AirPods 5 may also show up today, with reports pointing to a new chip, plus better health sensors and controls. The camera-equipped AirPods described in other leaks are reportedly planned for 2027 instead, which makes them unlikely to appear at today’s event. New Apple TV and HomePod hardware have also come up in previews, though the evidence behind those two is weaker than the evidence supporting the iPhone and Watch predictions.
What happens after the Apple event
Apple usually opens orders within days of a September iPhone event and starts deliveries about a week after that. In 2023, Apple announced the iPhone 15 Pro on September 12. Preorders opened three days later, and sales began on September 22. In 2024, the iPhone 16 family reached stores on September 20, a week after preorders opened. In 2025, Apple announced the iPhone 17 Pro on September 9. Preorders opened on September 12, and the phone became available a week later, on September 19.
Going by that pattern, the iPhone 18 Pro should become available around Friday, September 18. Reports disagree on whether preorders open on Friday, September 11, or Saturday, September 12, though several recent previews lean toward September 12 since September 11 falls outside Apple’s usual Friday preorder slot. Apple will confirm the actual schedule during the keynote and in its Newsroom posts afterwards.
The foldable iPhone might follow its own timeline. Bloomberg’s latest report says the device could start shipping in October, giving Apple room to announce it alongside the Pro models while giving its factories more time to build enough units. Limited early stock is also possible, so keep an eye on which countries make Apple’s first availability list, since new iPhones often reach one group of markets before expanding to others a week or two later.
Apple is also expected to share release dates for iOS 27 and watchOS 27, along with its other software updates. Based on past years, the main software updates should arrive during the week after the event, just before the new iPhones reach stores. Apple Watch orders may open on the same day as the keynote, with retail availability following alongside the iPhone 18 Pro models. Every date here stays provisional until Apple publishes it directly.
What to watch for during the keynote
A handful of questions will decide whether this event lives up to the buildup.
- What final name, price, and release date does Apple give its foldable iPhone?
- How does Apple adapt iOS to fit the bigger folding screen, including multitasking and app support
- Does the iPhone 18 Pro get a meaningful camera upgrade, or a smaller set of yearly improvements?
- Which products ship this September, and which ones move to October or spring 2027
The most likely outcome is a premium-focused event built around the iPhone 18 Pro line and Apple’s first foldable phone. Everything Apple has confirmed so far stops at the event’s name and time, plus how to watch it. Every product name, spec, price, and release date stays unofficial until Apple says it out loud at 10 a.m. Pacific time today.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: Anthropic researcher resigns, warns the AI race could end in human extinction
articles.text:
Crystal ball: What's more concerning than the prospect of AI bringing about the end of humanity? It's the people working at these companies making the same warning. Hours after a former OpenAI employee quit Anthropic and said, "No other human activity poses this level of danger," a colleague said there is more than a 10% chance that artificial intelligence could kill all humans within the next decade.
Jacob Coxon announced on X yesterday that he had resigned from Anthropic, having spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Dario Amodei's company. He was a member of AI's technical staff from July 2023 until he moved to Anthropic in July 2026.
"Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives," he wrote.
 – Jacob Coxon (@hilbertspaess) September 9, 2026
Coxon made several posts, none of which will ease the mind of anyone already worried about AI. He warned that the systems will soon become "superhuman" and able to hack anything.
There are plenty of other ominous lines in Coxon's posts, the most concerning likely being: "No other human activity poses this level of danger."
The researcher emphasized that both OpenAI and Anthropic are well aware of these risks. "The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade," he said.
 – Jacob Coxon (@hilbertspaess) September 9, 2026
So, why are companies continuing to develop these potentially extinction-causing models? The reason, according to the researcher, is this: "At OpenAI, many have not deeply internalized the civilizational stakes. At Anthropic, the stakes are well-understood, but they are locked in a race to get there first - they believe no one else will act responsibly, so they must do it themselves, despite the risk."
Coxon said some AI developers believe the technology could cause the end of all human life in the next few years, rather than decades, and that it was senior employees who were more concerned about these possibilities.
Evan Hubinger, an alignment science lead at Anthropic, responded to Coxon, and it wasn't very reassuring. He believes what he says is "correct," and that Anthropic has no plan for what to do if it happens.
"Jacob is correct here – we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to."
 – Evan Hubinger (@EvanHub) September 9, 2026
Hubinger said the risk from current models is low, but he was worried about superintelligence arising from recursive self-improvement. Anthropic issued the same warning in June.
The concept of AI killing everyone has moved from the stuff of sci-fi to a potential reality in recent times. Those fears were exacerbated following several incidents of AI agents going rogue, including the Hugging Face attack, the takeover of a German wiki, and an attempt to deceive real developers into approving malicious code.
Is there a solution? Coxon believes preventing a catastrophe may require a temporary ban on improving model capabilities, but it's unlikely that every, or any, AI company would agree to that measure.

articles.title: Problème mythique résolu par une IA : Terence Tao craint que la machine s'acharne sur des maths inutiles
articles.text:
Problème mythique résolu par une IA : Terence Tao craint que la machine s'acharne sur des maths inutiles
OpenAI vient d'annoncer la résolution d'un problème mathématique centenaire. Après la stupéfaction, une question essentielle est soulevée par Terence Tao, géant de la discipline : dépourvue d'intuition pour savoir où chercher, l'IA ne risque-t-elle pas de brûler une énergie colossale pour résoudre des milliers de théorèmes sans aucun intérêt ?
En déployant un essaim de 10 000 agents IA travaillant en parallèle pendant 88 heures, OpenAI a secoué le monde de la recherche mathématique en revendiquant la résolution de l’un des sept problèmes du prix du millénaire : les équations de Navier-Stokes.
Un exploit spectaculaire, facturé en millions de dollars de puissance de calcul, qui semble marquer le début d'une nouvelle ère. Pourtant, derrière l'effet d'annonce, l'analyse d'experts comme la médaille Fields Terence Tao invite à un enthousiasme beaucoup plus nuancé. Si les machines savent désormais franchir la ligne d'arrivée à toute vitesse, elles ne savent toujours pas choisir leur course.
On pourra d'ailleurs noter une ironie mordante : la résolution d'un problème du millénaire rapporte un million de dollars, pourtant, il en aura coûté beaucoup plus à OpenAI pour en venir à bout. La société ne revendique d'ailleurs pas la récompense.
Sur la forme, c'est un exploit retentissant
Rédigées au XIXe siècle, les équations de Navier-Stokes sont au cœur de notre compréhension de la physique moderne. Elles décrivent le mouvement des fluides : du flux sanguin dans nos artères au déplacement des masses d'air météo, en passant par l'aérodynamisme d'un avion.
Le problème ? Personne n'avait réussi à prouver mathématiquement si ces équations restaient toujours valides ou si elles finissaient par s'effondrer sous l'effet de singularités (des points où la vitesse devient théoriquement infinie, alors même que l'énergie reste finie).
En générant une démonstration de 166 pages – immédiatement formalisée et vérifiée dans le langage informatique Lean – l'architecture d'OpenAI montre l'apparition d'un tel effondrement (un finite-time blowup) sous certaines conditions imposées par des forces externes. Réussir à verrouiller une démonstration d'une telle complexité analytique en moins de quatre jours constitue une étape historique pour l’informatique.
Pour Terence Tao la force brute de l'IA n'a pas de boussole
Mais au-delà de la performance brute, que nous dit cette avancée sur l'intelligence réelle des machines ? C'est là que l'éclairage de Terence Tao, considéré comme l'un des plus grands mathématiciens vivants, devient essentiel.
Tao ne nie pas la puissance de ces outils – il les utilise lui-même au quotidien. En revanche, il souligne une limite structurelle fondamentale : les IA ne savent pas où chercher.
- L'exploration aveugle vs l'intuition conceptuelle
Pour un chercheur humain, la résolution d'un problème passe d'abord par la construction d'un cadre conceptuel. On cherche à comprendre pourquoi deux domaines en apparence éloignés (comme la théorie des nombres et la géométrie) pourraient se croiser. L’IA, elle, excelle dans la “force brute ciblée” : une fois qu'un couloir de recherche prometteur lui est indiqué, elle déploie une puissance phénoménale pour tester des millions de combinaisons algébriques et ajuster les bornes techniques. Sans guidage ou sans l'amorce de conjectures préalables (souvent issues de travaux humains), elle s'égarerait dans un espace d'états infini.
- Le risque de la preuve “stérile”
En mathématiques pures, la valeur d'une démonstration ne réside pas seulement dans le résultat final (la réponse Oui/Non), mais dans les concepts intermédiaires créés pour y parvenir. Une IA pourrait ainsi dépenser beaucoup d'énergie pour produire un résultat en lui-même peu intéressant, alors qu'une découverte porteuse proviendrait d'un autre chemin emprunté.
- Le navigateur et le moteur
Dans la vision de Terence Tao, la frontière ne s'efface pas, elle se déplace. L'humain conserve le rôle crucial du navigateur : celui qui possède la boussole, perçoit la structure profonde du paysage mathématique et formule la stratégie. L'IA devient le moteur d'exécution ultra-puissant qui défriche la forêt à une vitesse surhumaine.
Une science boostée par l'IA, pas dirigée par elle
L'annonce d'OpenAI sur Navier-Stokes valide le modèle d'une recherche scientifique accélérée par l'IA. Mais elle montre aussi ses limites économiques et théoriques : engloutir des millions de dollars d'électricité pour miner une preuve ne remplace pas l'étincelle conceptuelle.
L'IA n'a donc pas rendu les mathématiciens obsolètes. Elle pourrait surtout leur permettre de consacrer leur précieux temps à ce qu'ils font de mieux qu'elle : choisir les bonnes questions, trouver les bonnes idées et comprendre pourquoi une démonstration est importante. Un travail d'architecte, en somme.

This $502 4TB Crucial T705 is the cheapest Gen 5 SSD you can buy right now for just 12.5 cents per GB — ultra-fast storage upgrade with unreal 14,500 MB/s speeds is $181 less than a month ago, hitting its lowest price since February
The cheapest 4TB PCIe 5.0 SSD you can pick up right now
We've seen huge price rises this year for PC hardware, but RAM and SSDs have been especially affected. The global DRAM shortage, mostly caused by AI data center demands hoovering up all of the available stock, has caused prices to skyrocket. That's why this 4TB Crucial T705 SSD, down to $502.51, is a good deal in the current market, especially given its high capacity.
● Check out this deal at Amazon
Looking at Camelcamelcamel's price data, we can see that this drive was hitting almost $700 just a few weeks ago. Several price drops since have meant that the 4TB Crucial T705 is now almost below $500 for the first time in February. Along with a decent price drop, this Crucial drive is now the cheapest Gen 5 SSD you can pick up, with the next-cheapest model, the Samsung 990 Evo Plus, $60 more expensive at the moment.
It's not even a fair comparison, too, as the entry-level 990 Evo Plus only supports PCIe 5.0 over two lanes, not four, meaning you're only getting Gen 4-equivalent speeds. The Crucial T705 is a high-performance drive that's much faster, and right now, much cheaper.
This Crucial T705 4TB SSD is the cheapest Gen 5 SSD on the market right now. It offers read and write speeds of up to 14,500 MB/s and 12,700 MB/s apiece.
SSDs that offer Gen 5 speeds are a real step up over their slower Gen 4 counterparts. The T705 will offer you sequential read and write speeds of 14,500 MB/s and 12,700 MB/s, which is significantly faster than the fastest Gen 4 SSD on the market, the Samsung 990 Pro, which taps out at 7,450 MB/s. The T705 ships with 232-Layer Micro TLC memory modules and uses the Phison E26 controller.
It's also one of the fastest you can buy, period, rivalling the WD_Black SN8100, which hits speeds of 15,000 MB/s. That drive will set you back $659.99 right now, too, a significant increase compared to the deal on offer here. The Crucial T705 drive scored an Editor's Choice award for its sustained read/write performance at high speed, along with 4.5 stars in our review.
While we wished that SSD prices were back down to what we saw 18 months ago, it's good to see that high-performance drives like this one can still drop in price. The $502.51 sale price for this Crucial T705 4TB SSD is a seriously good one in the current market, and you won't be able to beat it for speed or price. Grab it at this price while you can.

articles.title: Apple Store sai do ar antes de evento do iPhone 18 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple Store sai do ar antes de evento do iPhone 18
Loja online da Apple está indisponível enquanto a empresa prepara o site para os anúncios desta quarta-feira (9).
A Apple Store está fora do ar na manhã desta quarta-feira (09/09). A empresa costuma desativar temporariamente a loja antes de grandes lançamentos, em preparação para a chegada de novos produtos. Às 14h de hoje, a companhia deve revelar novos iPhones, incluindo um inédito modelo dobrável.
Além disso, a Apple deve anunciar um novo chip de 2 nanômetros para os modelos Pro e melhorias no conjunto de câmeras do iPhone 18 Pro Max. Os preços também devem subir em relação à geração atual. O Tecnoblog acompanha a apresentação em tempo real.
Este será o primeiro evento comandado pelo novo CEO John Ternus, que sucede Tim Cook à frente da Apple. Ternus assume o cargo após 25 anos de bagagem, atuando como designer de produto e vice-presidente de engenharia de hardware.
O evento será transmitido ao vivo pelo site da Apple, pelo aplicativo Apple TV e pelo YouTube. Diferentemente dos anos anteriores, porém, a apresentação deve se concentrar nos modelos mais caros da família. O iPhone 18 base e o iPhone 18e são esperados apenas para o início de 2027.
